lessons.title: 1.1 Introducing Myself
lessons.notes_html:
Greetings in the Classroom

  • When the teacher comes into the class, she says: Assalam-o-Alaikum, students.
  • The students stand up and reply: Walekum-o-Salaam, teacher.
  • The teacher says: Thank you all. Please, sit down.
  • The students say: Thank you, teacher, and sit down.

Telling Your Name

  • The teacher says: My name is Asma. I am your teacher.
  • Kabir says: My name is Kabir. I am your student, teacher.
  • Sara says: My name is Sara. I am your student.
  • Ali says: Teacher, my name is Ali. I am also your student.
  • To tell our own name, we say: My name is ...

Key Points

  • We stand up to greet the teacher.
  • We tell our name with the words: My name is ...
  • Asma is the teacher in this lesson.

mcqs.q: When the teacher says Assalam-o-Alaikum, what do the students reply?
mcqs.why: The students stand up and reply Walekum-o-Salaam when the teacher greets them in the classroom.

mcqs.q: What is the name of the teacher in this lesson?
mcqs.why: The teacher tells her own name in the lesson: My name is Asma. I am your teacher.

mcqs.q: Kabir says: My name is ______.
mcqs.why: Kabir tells his own name, so he says: My name is Kabir. I am your student, teacher.

mcqs.q: What do the students say when the teacher asks them to sit down?
mcqs.why: The students say Thank you, teacher, and then they sit down quietly on their seats.

mcqs.q: Who is a student in this lesson?
mcqs.why: Sara says: My name is Sara. I am your student. Asma is the teacher of the class.

mcqs.q: To tell our own name, we say:
mcqs.why: When we tell our own name, we say My name is, and then we say our own name.

mcqs.q: When the teacher comes into the class, the students should:
mcqs.why: The students stand up to greet the teacher when she enters the classroom in the morning.

mcqs.q: Ali says: I am also your ______.
mcqs.why: Ali says: Teacher, my name is Ali. I am also your student, just like Kabir and Sara.

mcqs.q: The teacher says: I am your ______.
mcqs.why: Asma says: My name is Asma. I am your teacher. She teaches Kabir, Sara and Ali.

mcqs.q: After the greeting, the teacher asks the students to:
mcqs.why: The teacher says: Thank you all students. Please, sit down, and the students sit down.

lessons.title: 1.2 Alphabet Train
lessons.notes_html:
The Alphabet Train

  • The Alphabet Train has one coach for every letter from A to Z.
  • Every coach carries one picture.
  • The picture starts with the sound of the letter written on its coach.

Letter Pictures

  • A apple, B ball, C cat, D dog
  • E egg, F fish, G goat, H hen
  • I insect, J jug, K kettle, L lamp
  • M mango, N nose, O ox, P pencil
  • Q queen, R ring, S star, T tree
  • U umbrella, V violin, W watch, X x-ray
  • Y yolk, Z zebra

Key Points

  • The English alphabet has 26 letters.
  • Every picture on the train begins with the sound of its letter.

mcqs.q: Which picture goes with the letter A on the Alphabet Train?
mcqs.why: The coach of letter A carries the picture of an apple, because apple starts with the sound of A.

mcqs.q: The coach of letter B carries the picture of a:
mcqs.why: On the Alphabet Train, letter B carries a ball, because ball starts with the sound of B.

mcqs.q: Which letter has the picture of a cat?
mcqs.why: Cat starts with the letter C, so the picture of the cat is on the coach of letter C.

mcqs.q: The picture of an egg goes with the letter:
mcqs.why: Egg starts with the letter E, so the egg picture is on the coach of letter E.

mcqs.q: Letter M carries the picture of a:
mcqs.why: Mango starts with the letter M, so the mango picture is on the coach of letter M.

mcqs.q: Which picture goes with the letter Z?
mcqs.why: Zebra starts with the letter Z, so the zebra picture is on the last coach, letter Z.

mcqs.q: The picture of an umbrella is on the coach of letter:
mcqs.why: Umbrella starts with the letter U, so its picture is on the coach of letter U.

mcqs.q: How many letters are there in the English alphabet?
mcqs.why: The Alphabet Train has 26 coaches, one for every letter of the alphabet, from A to Z.

mcqs.q: Letter Q carries the picture of a:
mcqs.why: Queen starts with the letter Q, so the queen picture is on the coach of letter Q.

mcqs.q: Which letter comes with the picture of a fish?
mcqs.why: Fish starts with the letter F, so the fish picture is on the coach of letter F.

lessons.title: 1.3 Introducing Alphabets Aa, Bb, Cc, Dd
lessons.notes_html:
Meet the Letters

  • Aa — apple, arm, ant. A sounds aa as in apple.
  • Bb — ball, balloon, book. B sounds ba as in ball.
  • Cc — cat, candle, car. C sounds ka as in cat.
  • Dd — dog, doll, duck. D sounds da as in dog.

Tracing and Writing Practice

  • This lesson has tracing practice: we follow the dotted lines slowly to learn the shape of each letter.
  • Every letter has two forms: a capital letter (A, B, C, D) and a small letter (a, b, c, d).
  • The capital and the small letter have the same sound; only the shape and size are different.

First Letters of Pictures

  • Apple starts with a. Ball starts with b.
  • Car starts with c. Doll starts with d.
  • The first sound of a word tells us its first letter.

Key Points

  • Aa, Bb, Cc and Dd are the first four letters of the alphabet.
  • We trace the dotted letters to learn their shapes.

mcqs.q: Which word starts with the letter A?
mcqs.why: Apple starts with the letter A. Ball starts with B, cat with C and dog with D.

mcqs.q: What is the small letter of B?
mcqs.why: Capital B has the small letter b. The capital and small letters have the same name and sound.

mcqs.q: Which three picture words are given for the letter C?
mcqs.why: The book gives cat, candle and car for the letter C. All three words start with C.

mcqs.q: The letter D sounds da as in:
mcqs.why: The book says D sounds da as in dog. Dog, doll and duck are the picture words of D.

mcqs.q: Which letter comes after B?
mcqs.why: The alphabet goes in a fixed order: A, B, C, D. The letter after B is C.

mcqs.q: What is the capital letter of small c?
mcqs.why: Small c and capital C are the same letter. Only the shape and the size are different.

mcqs.q: Which picture word starts with the letter b?
mcqs.why: Balloon starts with the letter b. Apple starts with a, car with c and duck with d.

mcqs.q: In the tracing activity, we follow the:
mcqs.why: We trace the letters by following the dotted lines slowly, to learn the right shape of each letter.

mcqs.q: Which word starts with the letter d?
mcqs.why: Doll starts with the letter d. Candle starts with c, arm with a and book with b.

mcqs.q: The letter A sounds aa as in:
mcqs.why: The book says A sounds aa as in apple. Apple, arm and ant are the picture words of A.

lessons.title: 1.4 Introducing Alphabets Ee, Ff, Gg, Hh
lessons.notes_html:
Meet the Letters

  • Ee — egg, eye, ear. E sounds ee as in egg.
  • Ff — fish, fan, flower. F sounds fa as in fish.
  • Gg — goat, glass, gate. G sounds ga as in goat.
  • Hh — hen, house, horse. H sounds ha as in hen.

Tracing and Writing Practice

  • This lesson has tracing practice: first we follow the dotted letter with the starting arrow, then we write the same letter again without dots.
  • Every letter has a capital form (E, F, G, H) and a small form (e, f, g, h).

First Letters of Pictures

  • Egg starts with e. Fan starts with f.
  • Glass starts with g. Hen starts with h.
  • Saying the word slowly helps us hear its first sound.

Key Points

  • Ee, Ff, Gg and Hh come after Dd in the alphabet.
  • We look at the shape of the capital letter to find its small letter.

mcqs.q: Which three picture words are given for the letter E?
mcqs.why: The book gives egg, eye and ear for the letter E. All three words start with E.

mcqs.q: The letter F sounds fa as in:
mcqs.why: The book says F sounds fa as in fish. Fish, fan and flower are the picture words of F.

mcqs.q: Which word starts with the letter g?
mcqs.why: Glass starts with the letter g. Egg starts with e, fan with f and hen with h.

mcqs.q: What is the small letter of H?
mcqs.why: Capital H has the small letter h. Both letters have the same name and the same sound.

mcqs.q: The pictures in this lesson are an egg, a fan, a glass and a hen. The hen starts with:
mcqs.why: Hen starts with the letter h, so in the activity we encircle h for the picture of the hen.

mcqs.q: Which letter comes after F?
mcqs.why: The alphabet goes in a fixed order: E, F, G, H. The letter after F is G.

mcqs.q: Which word starts with the letter e?
mcqs.why: Ear starts with the letter e. Flower starts with f, gate with g and house with h.

mcqs.q: In tracing, after following the dotted letter, we:
options: write the letter again without dots
mcqs.why: First we follow the dotted letter with the starting arrow, and then we write the same letter again in the next line without dots.

mcqs.q: The letter G sounds ga as in:
mcqs.why: The book says G sounds ga as in goat. Goat, glass and gate are the picture words of G.

mcqs.q: What is the capital letter of small f?
mcqs.why: Small f and capital F are the same letter. Only the shape and the size are different.

lessons.title: 1.5 Introducing Alphabets Ii, Jj, Kk, Ll
lessons.notes_html:
Meet the Letters

  • Ii — insect, iron, inkpot. I sounds ii as in inkpot.
  • Jj — jug, jacket, jeep. J sounds ja as in jug.
  • Kk — kettle, kite, key. K sounds ka as in kite.
  • Ll — lamp, lion, leaf. L sounds la as in lamp.

Tracing and Writing Practice

  • This lesson has tracing practice of the letters Ii, Jj, Kk and Ll in small and capital forms.
  • Small i and small j have a dot on top. We put the dot after drawing the line of the letter.
  • Small i and small l look alike: small i has a dot, small l has no dot.

First Letters of Pictures

  • Iron starts with i. Jeep starts with j.
  • Kite starts with k. Leaf starts with l.

Key Points

  • Ii, Jj, Kk and Ll come after Hh in the alphabet.
  • Small i and small j carry a dot on top.

mcqs.q: Which three picture words are given for the letter J?
mcqs.why: The book gives jug, jacket and jeep for the letter J. All three words start with J.

mcqs.q: The letter K sounds ka as in:
mcqs.why: The book says K sounds ka as in kite. Kettle, kite and key are the picture words of K.

mcqs.q: Which small letter has a dot on top?
mcqs.why: Small i has a dot on top, and small j has a dot too. Small l looks like i but has no dot.

mcqs.q: The picture of an iron starts with the letter:
mcqs.why: Iron starts with the letter i, so in the activity we encircle i for the picture of the iron.

mcqs.q: What is the capital letter of small l?
mcqs.why: Small l and capital L are the same letter. We check the dot to tell small l from small i.

mcqs.q: Which word starts with the letter k?
mcqs.why: Kettle starts with the letter k. Jug starts with j, leaf with l and inkpot with i.

mcqs.q: Which letter comes after J?
mcqs.why: The alphabet goes in a fixed order: I, J, K, L. The letter after J is K.

mcqs.q: The letter L sounds la as in:
mcqs.why: The book says L sounds la as in lamp. Lamp, lion and leaf are the picture words of L.

mcqs.q: Which word starts with the letter j?
mcqs.why: Jeep starts with the letter j. Iron starts with i, kite with k and leaf with l.

mcqs.q: What is the small letter of I?
mcqs.why: Capital I has the small letter i, and small i always carries a dot on its top.

lessons.title: 1.6 Introducing Alphabets Mm, Nn, Oo, Pp
lessons.notes_html:
Meet the Letters

  • Mm — mango, monkey, mug. M sounds ma as in mango.
  • Nn — nose, nest, net. N sounds na as in nose.
  • Oo — ox, orange, onion. O sounds oo as in onion.
  • Pp — pencil, parrot, pilot. P sounds pa as in pencil.

Tracing and Writing Practice

  • This lesson has tracing practice of the letters Mm, Nn, Oo and Pp in small and capital forms.
  • Small o and capital O are round like a ball; we draw them in one round stroke.
  • Small m has two humps and small n has one hump. We count the humps to tell them apart.

First Letters of Pictures

  • Mango starts with m. Nose starts with n.
  • Orange starts with o. Parrot starts with p.

Key Points

  • Mm, Nn, Oo and Pp come after Ll in the alphabet.
  • Small m has two humps; small n has one hump.

mcqs.q: Which three picture words are given for the letter N?
mcqs.why: The book gives nose, nest and net for the letter N. All three words start with N.

mcqs.q: The letter M sounds ma as in:
mcqs.why: The book says M sounds ma as in mango. Mango, monkey and mug are the picture words of M.

mcqs.q: How many humps does small m have?
mcqs.why: Small m has two humps and small n has one hump. We count the humps to tell them apart.

mcqs.q: The picture of an orange starts with the letter:
mcqs.why: Orange starts with the letter o, so in the activity we encircle o for the picture of the orange.

mcqs.q: What is the small letter of P?
mcqs.why: Capital P has the small letter p. The capital and small letters have the same name and sound.

mcqs.q: Which word starts with the letter n?
mcqs.why: Nest starts with the letter n. Mug starts with m, onion with o and parrot with p.

mcqs.q: Which letter comes after O?
mcqs.why: The alphabet goes in a fixed order: M, N, O, P. The letter after O is P.

mcqs.q: The letter O sounds oo as in:
mcqs.why: The book says O sounds oo as in onion. Ox, orange and onion are the picture words of O.

mcqs.q: Which letter is round like a ball?
mcqs.why: Small o and capital O are round like a ball, and we draw them in one round stroke.

mcqs.q: The picture of a parrot starts with the letter:
mcqs.why: Parrot starts with the letter p, so in the activity we encircle p for the picture of the parrot.

lessons.title: 1.7 Introducing Alphabets Qq, Rr, Ss, Tt, Uu
lessons.notes_html:
Meet the Letters

  • Qq — queen, quilt, queue. Q sounds qu as in queen.
  • Rr — ring, rabbit, robot. R sounds ra as in ring.
  • Ss — star, soap, sun. S sounds sa as in sun.
  • Tt — tree, tap, table. T sounds ta as in tree.
  • Uu — umbrella, umpire, urn. U sounds aa as in umbrella.

Tracing and Writing Practice

  • This lesson has tracing practice of the letters Qq, Rr, Ss, Tt and Uu in small and capital forms.
  • Small s is drawn like a small snake, going first to the left and then to the right.
  • The small letter always has the same name and sound as its capital letter.

First Letters of Pictures

  • Queen starts with q. Rabbit starts with r. Sun starts with s.
  • Tree starts with t. Umpire starts with u.

Key Points

  • This lesson teaches five letters: Qq, Rr, Ss, Tt and Uu.
  • Small s is drawn like a small snake.

mcqs.q: Which three picture words are given for the letter S?
mcqs.why: The book gives star, soap and sun for the letter S. All three words start with S.

mcqs.q: The letter Q sounds qu as in:
mcqs.why: The book says Q sounds qu as in queen. Queen, quilt and queue are the picture words of Q.

mcqs.q: Small s is drawn like a:
mcqs.why: Small s is drawn like a small snake, going first to the left and then to the right.

mcqs.q: The picture of an umpire starts with the letter:
mcqs.why: Umpire starts with the letter u, so in the activity we encircle u for the picture of the umpire.

mcqs.q: Which word starts with the letter r?
mcqs.why: Rabbit starts with the letter r. Queen starts with q, sun with s and table with t.

mcqs.q: Which letter comes after S?
mcqs.why: The alphabet goes in a fixed order: Q, R, S, T, U. The letter after S is T.

mcqs.q: The letter T sounds ta as in:
mcqs.why: The book says T sounds ta as in tree. Tree, tap and table are the picture words of T.

mcqs.q: What is the capital letter of small u?
mcqs.why: Small u and capital U are the same letter. The small letter has the same name and sound as its capital.

mcqs.q: Which word starts with the letter q?
mcqs.why: Quilt starts with the letter q. Robot starts with r, soap with s and tap with t.

mcqs.q: The picture of the sun starts with the letter:
mcqs.why: Sun starts with the letter s, so in the activity we encircle s for the picture of the sun.

lessons.title: 1.8 Introducing Alphabets Vv, Ww, Xx, Yy, Zz
lessons.notes_html:
Meet the Letters

  • Vv — violin, vest, van. V sounds va as in van.
  • Ww — watch, window, wall. W sounds wa as in watch.
  • Xx — x-ray, box, fox. X sounds ks as in box.
  • Yy — yolk, yarn, yoyo. Y sounds ya as in yolk.
  • Zz — zebra, zip, zoo. Z sounds za as in zebra.

Tracing and Writing Practice

  • This lesson has tracing practice of the last five letters of the alphabet.
  • Small w is like two small v letters joined together.
  • Small x is made of two crossing lines.
  • In the word box, the letter x comes at the end of the word.

First Letters of Pictures

  • Van starts with v. Watch starts with w. Yolk starts with y. Zebra starts with z.
  • The word box has the letter x at its end.

Key Points

  • Vv, Ww, Xx, Yy and Zz are the last five letters of the alphabet.
  • Now we know all 26 letters from A to Z.

mcqs.q: Which three picture words are given for the letter W?
mcqs.why: The book gives watch, window and wall for the letter W. All three words start with W.

mcqs.q: The letter Z sounds za as in:
mcqs.why: The book says Z sounds za as in zebra. Zebra, zip and zoo are the picture words of Z.

mcqs.q: In the word box, the letter x is at the:
mcqs.why: Box does not begin with x. The letter x comes at the end of the word box.

mcqs.q: Small w is like:
mcqs.why: Small w is like two small v letters joined together, and small x is made of two crossing lines.

mcqs.q: Which word starts with the letter v?
mcqs.why: Van starts with the letter v. Watch starts with w, yolk with y and zebra with z.

mcqs.q: Which letter is the last letter of the alphabet?
mcqs.why: Z is the last letter of the alphabet. These are the last five letters: V, W, X, Y, Z.

mcqs.q: The letter Y sounds ya as in:
mcqs.why: The book says Y sounds ya as in yolk. Yolk, yarn and yoyo are the picture words of Y.

mcqs.q: Small x is made of:
mcqs.why: Small x is made of two crossing lines. We cross one line over the other to write x.

mcqs.q: The picture of a watch starts with the letter:
mcqs.why: Watch starts with the letter w, so in the activity we encircle w for the picture of the watch.

mcqs.q: The letter X sounds ks as in:
mcqs.why: The book says X sounds ks as in box. X-ray, box and fox are the picture words of X.

lessons.title: 1.9 Revision
lessons.notes_html:
Capital and Small Letters

  • This is a revision lesson: we read the whole alphabet again and write the missing capital and small letters.
  • Every letter has a pair: A a, B b, C c and so on up to Z z.
  • When only the small letter is given, we write its capital; when only the capital is given, we write its small letter.

After, Before and Between

  • After: c–d, s–t, p–q, l–m, f–g, j–k, m–n, o–p, e–f, b–c, h–i, k–l.
  • Before: A comes before B, T before U, L before M, N before O, X before Y.
  • Between: a–b–c, l–m–n, d–e–f, p–q–r, g–h–i, s–t–u, j–k–l, v–w–x, m–n–o, e–f–g, x–y–z.
  • The alphabet always goes in the same order, so we only have to remember the order once.

Key Points

  • Revision means learning the same thing once more.
  • Every capital letter has its own small letter.

mcqs.q: What comes after the letter c?
mcqs.why: The alphabet goes in a fixed order: a, b, c, d. The letter after c is d.

mcqs.q: What comes before the letter U?
mcqs.why: The alphabet goes in a fixed order: S, T, U, V. The letter before U is T.

mcqs.q: What comes between a and c?
mcqs.why: The three letters go together in order: a, b, c. So b comes between a and c.

mcqs.q: What is the small letter of G?
mcqs.why: Capital G has the small letter g. Every capital letter has its own small letter.

mcqs.q: What is the capital letter of small m?
mcqs.why: Small m and capital M are the same letter. Only the shape and the size are different.

mcqs.q: What comes after the letter p?
mcqs.why: The alphabet goes in a fixed order: o, p, q, r. The letter after p is q.

mcqs.q: What comes between s and u?
mcqs.why: The three letters go together in order: s, t, u. So t comes between s and u.

mcqs.q: What comes before the letter B?
mcqs.why: A is the first letter of the alphabet, and it comes just before the letter B.

mcqs.q: What comes between x and z?
mcqs.why: The last three letters go in order: x, y, z. So y comes between x and z.

mcqs.q: What comes between l and n?
mcqs.why: The three letters go together in order: l, m, n. So m comes between l and n.

lessons.title: 1.10 Initial Sounds
lessons.notes_html:
The First Sound of a Word

  • The initial sound of a word is the sound we hear at its very beginning.
  • Apple — a, ball — b, car — c, house — h, goat — g, insect — i.
  • Flower — f, egg — e, net — n, parrot — p, rabbit — r, queen — q.

Coloured Letters in Words

  • Some coloured letters are at the start of the word: doll — d, fan — f, onion — o, pencil — p, van — v, tree — t, window — w.
  • Some coloured letters are at the end of the word: jeep — p, mango — o, nest — t, kettle — l, monkey — y.
  • We look at the whole word carefully to find the coloured letter.

Key Points

  • The first letter of a word gives its initial sound.
  • A coloured letter can be at the start or at the end of a word.

mcqs.q: What is the initial (first) letter of the word house?
mcqs.why: House begins with the letter h. The initial sound of a word is the sound at its very beginning.

mcqs.q: What is the initial letter of the word queen?
mcqs.why: Queen begins with the letter q. We hear the q sound at the very start of the word.

mcqs.q: What is the initial letter of the word insect?
mcqs.why: Insect begins with the letter i. The first letter of a word gives its initial sound.

mcqs.q: What is the initial letter of the word flower?
mcqs.why: Flower begins with the letter f. Say the word slowly and hear the first sound.

mcqs.q: What is the initial letter of the word net?
mcqs.why: Net begins with the letter n. The letter at the start of the word is its initial letter.

mcqs.q: What is the initial letter of the word goat?
mcqs.why: Goat begins with the letter g. The initial sound of goat is the g sound.

mcqs.q: What is the initial letter of the word parrot?
mcqs.why: Parrot begins with the letter p. We hear the p sound at the very beginning of the word.

mcqs.q: What is the initial letter of the word egg?
mcqs.why: Egg begins with the letter e. The first sound of the word egg is the e sound.

mcqs.q: What is the initial letter of the word rabbit?
mcqs.why: Rabbit begins with the letter r. The initial letter is always the first letter of the word.

mcqs.q: The sound we hear at the very beginning of a word is called its:
mcqs.why: The initial sound of a word is the sound we hear at its very beginning, like a in apple.

lessons.title: 1.11 Ending Sounds
lessons.notes_html:
Words Ending with t and n

  • Bat, hat, cat and net all end with the letter t. Their ending sound is t.
  • Pen, hen, van and fan all end with the letter n. Their ending sound is n.

Words Ending with p and r

  • Cup, ship, lamp and zip all end with the letter p.
  • Star, car, flower and jar all end with the letter r.
  • Words that end with the same letter usually make the same ending sound.
  • If we say the words slowly, we can hear the ending sound clearly.

Key Points

  • The ending sound is the sound at the end of a word.
  • Words ending with the same letter have the same ending sound.

mcqs.q: With which letter does the word bat end?
mcqs.why: Bat ends with the letter t. Bat, hat, cat and net all end with the t sound.

mcqs.q: With which letter does the word hen end?
mcqs.why: Hen ends with the letter n. Pen, hen, van and fan all end with the n sound.

mcqs.q: With which letter does the word cup end?
mcqs.why: Cup ends with the letter p. Cup, ship, lamp and zip all end with the p sound.

mcqs.q: With which letter does the word star end?
mcqs.why: Star ends with the letter r. Star, car, flower and jar all end with the r sound.

mcqs.q: Which word ends with the letter n?
mcqs.why: Fan ends with the letter n. Bat ends with t, cup with p and star with r.

mcqs.q: Which word ends with the letter p?
mcqs.why: Zip ends with the letter p. Hat ends with t, car with r and pen with n.

mcqs.q: With which letter does the word ship end?
mcqs.why: Ship ends with the letter p, like cup, lamp and zip. Say the word slowly to hear it.

mcqs.q: With which letter does the word van end?
mcqs.why: Van ends with the letter n, like pen, hen and fan. Their ending sound is n.

mcqs.q: With which letter does the word jar end?
mcqs.why: Jar ends with the letter r, like star, car and flower. Their ending sound is r.

mcqs.q: Words that end with the same letter usually have the same:
mcqs.why: Words that end with the same letter usually make the same ending sound, like bat and hat.

lessons.title: 1.12 Making Words
lessons.notes_html:
Joining Two Letters

  • When we join two letter sounds quickly, they make one short sound chunk.
  • a+n = an, a+t = at, e+n = en, e+t = et, i+p = ip.
  • i+n = in, o+g = og, o+x = ox, u+g = ug, u+t = ut.

Joining Three Letters

  • v+a+n = van, b+a+t = bat, h+e+n = hen, n+e+t = net.
  • z+i+p = zip, p+i+n = pin, d+o+g = dog, b+o+x = box.
  • j+u+g = jug, h+u+t = hut.
  • First we say the sound of each letter, then we run the sounds together to read the word.

Key Points

  • Joining letter sounds makes words.
  • We read the word first and then find the picture of the same thing.

mcqs.q: Join the letters: j + u + g. Which word do we make?
mcqs.why: We say the sounds j, u, g and run them together. The word we make is jug.

mcqs.q: Join the letters: d + o + g. Which word do we make?
mcqs.why: We say the sounds d, o, g and run them together. The word we make is dog.

mcqs.q: Join the letters: b + o + x. Which word do we make?
mcqs.why: We say the sounds b, o, x and run them together. The word we make is box.

mcqs.q: Join the letters: h + u + t. Which word do we make?
mcqs.why: We say the sounds h, u, t and run them together. The word we make is hut.

mcqs.q: Join the letters: v + a + n. Which word do we make?
mcqs.why: We say the sounds v, a, n and run them together. The word we make is van.

mcqs.q: Join the letters: p + i + n. Which word do we make?
mcqs.why: We say the sounds p, i, n and run them together. The word we make is pin.

mcqs.q: Join the letters: z + i + p. Which word do we make?
mcqs.why: We say the sounds z, i, p and run them together. The word we make is zip.

mcqs.q: Join the letters: a + n. Which sound chunk do we make?
mcqs.why: When we join the sounds a and n quickly, they become one short sound chunk: an.

mcqs.q: Join the letters: o + g. Which sound chunk do we make?
mcqs.why: When we join the sounds o and g quickly, they become one short sound chunk: og.

mcqs.q: Join the letters: h + e + n. Which word do we make?
mcqs.why: We say the sounds h, e, n and run them together. The word we make is hen.

lessons.title: 2.1 Basic Greetings
lessons.notes_html:
Saba Meets Areeba

  • Saba says: Good Morning, Areeba. How are you?
  • Areeba says: Good morning, Saba. I am fine.
  • Saba shows her sister and says: This is my sister, Aliya.
  • Areeba says: Hello! Aliya. My name is Areeba.

How We Greet

  • We greet our friends in the morning by saying Good morning.
  • We ask our friend: How are you?
  • The friend answers: I am fine.

Key Points

  • In the morning we say: Good morning.
  • Aliya is the sister of Saba.

mcqs.q: What does Saba ask Areeba?

mcqs.q: What does Areeba answer?
mcqs.why: Areeba says: Good morning, Saba. I am fine. She tells Saba that she is fine.

mcqs.q: Who is Aliya?
mcqs.why: Saba says: This is my sister, Aliya. So Aliya is the sister of Saba.

mcqs.q: In the morning, we greet our friends by saying:
mcqs.why: We greet our friends in the morning by saying good morning and asking how they are.

mcqs.q: Who says: This is my sister, Aliya?
mcqs.why: Saba shows her sister to Areeba and says: This is my sister, Aliya.

mcqs.q: Areeba tells Aliya: My name is ______.
mcqs.why: Areeba says: Hello! Aliya. My name is Areeba. She tells her own name to Aliya.

mcqs.q: Saba and Areeba meet in the:
mcqs.why: They say good morning to each other, so they meet in the morning time.

mcqs.q: When a friend asks How are you, we answer:
mcqs.why: Areeba answers the question How are you with the words: I am fine.

mcqs.q: How many girls are in this conversation?
mcqs.why: There are three girls: Saba, Areeba and Saba's sister Aliya, who is introduced in the lesson.

mcqs.q: We ask our friend ______ to know how he or she is.
mcqs.why: We ask our friend How are you, and the friend answers: I am fine.

lessons.title: 2.2 Vowels and Consonants
lessons.notes_html:
Vowels and Consonants

  • There are five vowels: a, e, i, o, u.
  • All the other twenty-one letters are consonants: b, c, d, f, g, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, q, r, s, t, v, w, x, y, z.
  • Every English word has at least one vowel sound in it.

Missing Letters

  • s(u)n — sun, (t)ap — tap, ti(n) — tin, t(r)ee — tree, l(i)on — lion.
  • d(o)ll — doll, soa(p) — soap, (p)arrot — parrot, y(a)rn — yarn.
  • (m)onkey — monkey, o(n)ion — onion, ki(t)e — kite.
  • The picture shows the thing, and the missing letter completes its name.

Words Starting with Vowels and Consonants

  • We write c for a word starting with a consonant: banana, girl, car, bus, pigeon, nest, lion.
  • We write v for a word starting with a vowel: arm, orange, egg, umbrella, inkpot.
  • We only look at the first letter of the word to decide.

Key Points

  • Vowels are only five: a, e, i, o, u.
  • The other 21 letters are consonants.

mcqs.q: How many vowels are there in the English alphabet?
mcqs.why: There are five vowels: a, e, i, o, u. All the other twenty-one letters are consonants.

mcqs.q: Which letter is a vowel?
mcqs.why: The vowels are a, e, i, o and u. The letters b, t and m are consonants.

mcqs.q: Which letter is a consonant?
mcqs.why: The letter n is a consonant. The letters a, e and i are vowels.

mcqs.q: Which letter is missing: s__n (sun)?
mcqs.why: The picture shows the sun. The missing letter is u, and the word is sun.

mcqs.q: Which word starts with a vowel?
mcqs.why: Arm starts with the vowel a, so we write v for it. Car, girl and bus start with consonants.

mcqs.q: Which letter is missing: __ap (tap)?
mcqs.why: The picture shows a tap. The missing first letter is t, and the word is tap.

mcqs.q: We write v before a word that starts with a:
mcqs.why: We write c for words starting with consonants and v for words starting with vowels.

mcqs.q: Which letter is missing: l__on (lion)?
mcqs.why: The picture shows a lion. The missing letter is i, and the word is lion.

mcqs.q: Which word starts with a consonant?
mcqs.why: Lion starts with the consonant l, so we write c for it. Egg, arm and onion start with vowels.

mcqs.q: Which letter is missing: ki__e (kite)?
mcqs.why: The picture shows a kite. The missing letter is t, and the word is kite.

lessons.title: 2.3 Common Consonant Digraphs
lessons.notes_html:
What Is a Digraph?

  • A digraph is two letters that make one sound.
  • In sh, the letters s and h together make one sound.
  • In ch, the letters c and h together make one different sound.

Words with sh

  • shop, shark, sheep, ship, shoe, shoulder.

Words with ch

  • chalk, chick, chair, chips, chin, chocolate, chain.

Missing Digraphs

  • __ip — ship (sh), __air — chair (ch), __eep — sheep (sh), __in — chin (ch).
  • __oe — shoe (sh), __ocolate — chocolate (ch), __ain — chain (ch), __oulder — shoulder (sh), __ark — shark (sh).
  • The picture tells us the word, and the word tells us whether it begins with sh or ch.

Key Points

  • A digraph is two letters making one sound.
  • sh words: ship, sheep, shark. ch words: chair, chick, chips.

mcqs.q: A digraph is two letters that make:
mcqs.why: A digraph is two letters that make one sound, like s and h together in the word ship.

mcqs.q: Which digraph is missing: __ip (ship)?
mcqs.why: The picture shows a ship. Ship begins with sh, so the missing digraph is sh.

mcqs.q: Which digraph is missing: __air (chair)?
mcqs.why: The picture shows a chair. Chair begins with ch, so the missing digraph is ch.

mcqs.q: The word sheep begins with:
mcqs.why: Sheep begins with the digraph sh. The letters s and h together make one sound.

mcqs.q: The word chocolate begins with:
mcqs.why: Chocolate begins with the digraph ch. The letters c and h together make one sound.

mcqs.q: Which word begins with ch?
mcqs.why: Chick begins with ch. Shop, sheep and ship all begin with the digraph sh.

mcqs.q: Which word begins with sh?
mcqs.why: Shark begins with sh. Chair, chin and chips all begin with the digraph ch.

mcqs.q: Which digraph is missing: __oe (shoe)?
mcqs.why: The picture shows a shoe. Shoe begins with sh, so the missing digraph is sh.

mcqs.q: Which digraph is missing: __ain (chain)?
mcqs.why: The picture shows a chain. Chain begins with ch, so the missing digraph is ch.

mcqs.q: In the digraph sh, the two letters are:
mcqs.why: In sh, the letters s and h together make one sound, as in shop, shark and sheep.

lessons.title: 2.4 Naming Words: Animals and Birds
lessons.notes_html:
Animals

  • The animals in this lesson are: goat, horse, lion, monkey, camel, cat, dog, donkey and cow.
  • Animals walk on the land.

Birds

  • The birds in this lesson are: hen, parrot, eagle, pigeon, sparrow, duck, crow, peacock and owl.
  • Birds have wings and can fly in the sky.

In the Jungle Picture

  • Near the pond we can see an elephant, a lion, a horse, a cow, a monkey, a deer, a giraffe, a bear, a leopard, a dog and a cat.
  • The birds in the picture are ducks, a crane, a peacock, a crow and a pigeon.
  • A naming word is the name of a person, place, animal or thing.

Key Points

  • Animals walk on land; birds have wings and fly.
  • Names of animals and birds are naming words.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a bird?
mcqs.why: A peacock is a bird. Birds have wings and can fly. Lion, horse and cow are animals.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an animal?
mcqs.why: A camel is an animal that walks on the land. Duck, crow and owl are birds.

mcqs.q: Birds can fly because they have:
mcqs.why: Birds have wings and can fly in the sky, while animals walk on the land.

mcqs.q: Which bird is named in this lesson?
mcqs.why: The birds in the lesson are hen, parrot, eagle, pigeon, sparrow, duck, crow, peacock and owl.

mcqs.why: The elephant is one of the animals in the big jungle picture near the pond.

mcqs.why: A dog is an animal, not a bird. Hen, duck and eagle are all birds with wings.

mcqs.why: The crane is one of the birds in the jungle picture, with the ducks, peacock, crow and pigeon.

mcqs.q: A monkey is an:
mcqs.why: A monkey is an animal. It is in the lesson list of animals with goat, horse, lion and camel.

lessons.title: 2.5 Naming Words: Fruits and Vegetables
lessons.notes_html:
Fruits

  • The fruits in this lesson are: apple, mango, banana, orange, melon and lemon.
  • Fruits are sweet, and we eat many of them raw.

Vegetables

  • The vegetables in this lesson are: carrot, potato, peas, onion, cabbage and tomato.
  • Vegetables are mostly cooked in food.

At the Bazaar

  • In the bazaar picture, a cart is full of fruits and vegetables.
  • We can choose the fruits and vegetables we like from the cart.

Key Points

  • Fruits are sweet; vegetables are mostly cooked.
  • Apple, mango and banana are fruits. Carrot, potato and onion are vegetables.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a fruit?

mcqs.why: Vegetables are mostly cooked in food. Fruits are sweet and we eat many of them raw.

lessons.title: 2.6 Syllable in Words
lessons.notes_html:
What Is a Syllable?

  • A syllable is a part of a word that contains a single vowel sound.
  • The word ball has one vowel sound, so it has one syllable.
  • The word balloon has two parts, bal-loon, and two vowel sounds, so it has two syllables.
  • We can clap once for ball and twice for balloon.

Say and Clap

  • Pot — one clap. Cat — one clap.
  • Parrot — two claps: par-rot. Kitten — two claps: kit-ten.
  • Clapping helps us count the parts of a word.

Sorting the Words

  • One syllable words: kite, tree, book, duck, tap.
  • Two syllable words: monkey (mon-key), orange (or-ange), apple (ap-ple), lion (li-on), pencil (pen-cil), window (win-dow), zebra (ze-bra).
  • We say each word slowly and count its vowel sounds to sort it.

Key Points

  • A syllable has one vowel sound.
  • Ball has one syllable; balloon has two.

mcqs.q: How many syllables does the word ball have?
mcqs.why: Ball has only one vowel sound, so it has one syllable. We clap once for ball.

mcqs.q: How many syllables does the word balloon have?
mcqs.why: Balloon is made of two parts, bal-loon, and has two vowel sounds, so it has two syllables.

mcqs.q: How many syllables does the word parrot have?
mcqs.why: Parrot gets two claps: par-rot. It has two parts and two vowel sounds.

mcqs.q: How many syllables does the word cat have?
mcqs.why: Cat gets one clap because it has one syllable, like the word pot.

mcqs.q: How many syllables does the word pencil have?
mcqs.why: Pencil has two syllables: pen-cil. We say the word slowly and count two vowel sounds.

mcqs.q: Which word has only one syllable?
mcqs.why: Book has one syllable. Monkey, apple and zebra each have two syllables.

mcqs.q: Which word has two syllables?
mcqs.why: Window has two syllables: win-dow. Kite, tree and tap each have one syllable.

mcqs.q: A syllable is a part of a word with a single ______ sound.
mcqs.why: A syllable is a part of a word that contains a single vowel sound, like ball with one and balloon with two.

mcqs.q: The word kitten is split as:
mcqs.why: Kitten gets two claps: kit-ten, because it has two syllables, like parrot.

mcqs.q: We count the syllables of a word by:
mcqs.why: Clapping helps us count the parts of a word. We clap once for ball and twice for balloon.

lessons.title: 2.7 Counting Numbers (Nursery Rhyme)
lessons.notes_html:
The Rhyme

  • One, two, three, four, five, once I caught a fish alive.
  • Six, seven, eight, nine, ten, then I let it go again.
  • The boy let the fish go because it bit his finger.
  • The fish bit the little finger on his right hand.
  • The rhyme teaches us the number words from one to ten.

Rhyming Words

  • five rhymes with alive. ten rhymes with again.
  • go rhymes with so. it rhymes with bit. right rhymes with bite.
  • Rhyming words end with the same sound.

Sets of Rhyming Words

  • bow, row, toe — all end with the same sound.
  • night, sight, kite — all end with the same sound.
  • pen, hen, ten — all end with the en sound.

Numbers in Words

  • 1 — one, 2 — two, 3 — three, 4 — four, 5 — five.
  • 6 — six, 7 — seven, 8 — eight, 9 — nine, 10 — ten.

Key Points

  • The boy caught a fish and let it go because it bit his finger.
  • Rhyming words end with the same sound.

mcqs.q: What did the boy catch in the rhyme?
mcqs.why: The rhyme says: One, two, three, four, five, once I caught a fish alive.

mcqs.q: Why did the boy let the fish go?
mcqs.why: The boy let the fish go again because the fish bit the little finger on his right hand.

mcqs.q: Which finger did the fish bite?
options: the little finger on his right hand
the thumb of his left hand
the first finger of his left hand
the little finger on his left hand
mcqs.why: The rhyme tells us the fish bit the little finger on the boy's right hand.

mcqs.q: Which word rhymes with five?
mcqs.why: Five rhymes with alive. Both words end with the same ive sound.

mcqs.q: Which word rhymes with ten?
mcqs.why: Ten rhymes with again in the rhyme: Six, seven, eight, nine, ten, then I let it go again.

mcqs.q: Which set of words rhyme with each other?
mcqs.why: Pen, hen and ten all end with the en sound, so they rhyme with each other.

mcqs.q: What is the number 7 in words?
mcqs.why: The number words go: six for 6, seven for 7, eight for 8 and nine for 9.

mcqs.q: What is the number 4 in words?
mcqs.why: The number words go: three for 3, four for 4 and five for 5. We learn these spellings by heart.

mcqs.q: Which word rhymes with right?
mcqs.why: Right rhymes with bite. Both words end with the same ite sound in the rhyme.

mcqs.q: The rhyme teaches us the number words from:
mcqs.why: The rhyme counts one, two, three, four, five and then six, seven, eight, nine, ten.

lessons.title: 2.8 A or AN
lessons.notes_html:
When to Use A

  • We use a before naming words that start with a consonant sound.
  • Examples: a cat, a van, a bag, a chair, a horse.

When to Use AN

  • We use an before naming words that start with a vowel sound.
  • Examples: an apple, an egg, an insect, an orange, an umpire.
  • We first listen to the first sound of the word and then choose a or an.

Practice Words

  • a car, an elephant, an inkpot, a window, a net, an eye.
  • a doll, an arm, a table, an elbow, a lion, an airplane.
  • a glass, an urn, a balloon, an onion.

Key Points

  • Use a before a consonant sound.
  • Use an before a vowel sound: a, e, i, o, u.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: ______ apple.
mcqs.why: Apple starts with the vowel sound a, so we use an before it: an apple.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: ______ cat.
mcqs.why: Cat starts with the consonant sound c, so we use a before it: a cat.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: ______ elephant.
mcqs.why: Elephant starts with the vowel sound e, so we use an before it: an elephant.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: ______ window.
mcqs.why: Window starts with the consonant sound w, so we use a before it: a window.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: ______ eye.
mcqs.why: Eye starts with a vowel sound, so we use an before it: an eye.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: ______ horse.
mcqs.why: Horse starts with the consonant sound h, so we use a before it: a horse.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: ______ urn.
mcqs.why: Urn starts with the vowel sound u, so we use an before it: an urn.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: ______ balloon.
mcqs.why: Balloon starts with the consonant sound b, so we use a before it: a balloon.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: ______ inkpot.
mcqs.why: Inkpot starts with the vowel sound i, so we use an before it: an inkpot.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: ______ table.
mcqs.why: Table starts with the consonant sound t, so we use a before it: a table.

lessons.title: 2.9 THIS and THAT
lessons.notes_html:
This for Near, That for Far

  • We use this for a thing that is near the speaker: This is a bag. This is a pencil. This is a chair.
  • We use that for a thing that is far from the speaker: That is a bag. That is a pencil. That is a chair.
  • Both this and that are used for one thing only.

In the Pictures

  • The woman feeding a hen near her says: This is a hen. The girl standing far says: That is a hen.
  • The girl holding a cup says: This is a cup. The boy pointing from far says: That is a cup.
  • The boy reading at the table says: This is a book. The boy at the door says: That is a book.

Key Points

  • This points to a near thing.
  • That points to a far thing.

mcqs.q: We use this for a thing that is:
mcqs.why: This is used to point out a thing that is near the speaker, like: This is a bag.

mcqs.q: We use that for a thing that is:
mcqs.why: That is used to point out a thing that is far from the speaker, like: That is a chair.

mcqs.q: A girl is holding a cup. She says:
mcqs.why: The cup is in her hand, near her, so the girl says: This is a cup.

mcqs.q: A boy is standing at the door and looking at a book on the table. He says:
mcqs.why: The book is far from the boy at the door, so he says: That is a book.

mcqs.q: This and that are used for how many things?
mcqs.why: Both this and that are used for one thing only, near or far.

mcqs.q: The woman is feeding a hen near her. She says:
options: It is a hen far away
mcqs.why: The hen is near the woman who feeds it, so she says: This is a hen.

mcqs.q: A boy is touching a chair. He says:
mcqs.why: The boy is touching the chair, so it is near him and he says: This is a chair.

mcqs.q: The boy is standing at the door, away from the chair. He says:
mcqs.why: The chair is far from the boy at the door, so he says: That is a chair.

mcqs.q: Which word do we use for a bag lying near the boy at his desk?
mcqs.why: The boy standing near the desk says: This is a bag, because the bag is near him.

mcqs.q: Which word do we use for a pencil lying far from the boy?
mcqs.why: The boy standing at the door says: That is a pencil, because the pencil is far from him.

lessons.title: 2.10 Singular and Plural
lessons.notes_html:
One and Many

  • Singular means one object or thing.
  • Plural means two or more objects or things.
  • We make the plural by adding s at the end of the word.

Singular and Plural Words

  • a cat — cats, a flower — flowers, an egg — eggs, a hat — hats.
  • a ball — balls, an umbrella — umbrellas, a hen — hens.
  • The letter s at the end tells us that there is more than one.

Counting the Objects

  • Two vans, five cups, three pens, seven flowers.
  • Six inkpots, nine books, five birds, eight dogs, four apples.
  • We count the pictures one by one and then write the number word with the plural word.

Key Points

  • Singular means one; plural means more than one.
  • We add s to make a plural: cat — cats.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of cat?
mcqs.why: We make the plural by adding s at the end: a cat — cats. The s tells us there is more than one.

mcqs.q: Singular means:
mcqs.why: Singular means one object or thing, and plural means two or more objects or things.

mcqs.q: To make a plural, we add the letter:
mcqs.why: We make the plural by adding s at the end: a flower — flowers, an egg — eggs.

mcqs.q: How many cups are counted in the picture activity?
mcqs.why: We count the pictures one by one: five cups. The number word is written with the plural word.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of hen?
mcqs.why: We add s to make the plural: a hen — hens, just like a hat — hats.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: nine ______.
mcqs.why: Nine is more than one, so we use the plural word books: nine books.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of umbrella?
mcqs.why: We add s at the end: an umbrella — umbrellas. The s shows there is more than one.

mcqs.q: How many dogs are counted in the picture activity?
mcqs.why: We count the dogs in the picture one by one: eight dogs.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of egg?
mcqs.why: We add s to make the plural: an egg — eggs, just like a ball — balls.

mcqs.q: The word vans in two vans is:
mcqs.why: Two vans means more than one van, so vans is a plural word. It ends with the letter s.

lessons.title: 2.11 Naming Words
lessons.notes_html:
What Is a Naming Word?

  • A naming word is the name of a person, place, animal or thing.
  • In this lesson we label the things in a room picture.

Things in the Room

  • The ceiling fan is labelled fan. The clock on the wall is the wall clock.
  • The curtained opening is the window. The school bag is on the desk.
  • The big screen is the television. The desk seat is the chair.
  • The red armchair is the sofa. The small light by the bed is the lamp.
  • The big wooden bed is the bed, and the soft thing under the head is the pillow.

Key Points

  • A naming word names a person, place, animal or thing.
  • Fan, lamp, bed and sofa are naming words.

mcqs.q: A naming word is the name of a:
mcqs.why: A naming word is the name of a person, place, animal or thing, like sofa, lamp and bag.

mcqs.q: The clock on the wall of the room is called a:
mcqs.why: The label on the clock on the wall says wall clock in the room picture.

mcqs.q: The big screen in the room is a:
mcqs.why: The label on the big screen in the room says television.

mcqs.q: We sleep on a:
mcqs.why: The label on the big wooden bed in the room says bed. We sleep on a bed.

mcqs.q: The soft thing under the head on the bed is a:
mcqs.why: The label on the soft thing under the head says pillow in the room picture.

mcqs.q: The school bag in the picture is on the:

mcqs.q: The small light by the bed is a:

mcqs.q: We sit on a:

lessons.title: 3.1 Social Courtesies
lessons.notes_html:
Kabir and Suman

  • Kabir finds a book and says: Excuse me, Suman, is this your book?
  • Suman says: Yes, Kabir. That is my book. Thank you.
  • Kabir says: You are welcome, Suman.

Polite Words

  • We say Excuse me to get the attention of a person.
  • We say Thank you when someone helps us.
  • We say You are welcome as the reply to thank you.

Key Points

  • Excuse me, Thank you and You are welcome are polite words.
  • Kabir returns the book of Suman.

mcqs.q: What does Kabir find?
mcqs.why: Kabir finds a book and asks Suman: Excuse me, Suman, is this your book?

mcqs.q: To get the attention of a person, we say:
mcqs.why: We say Excuse me to get attention, as Kabir does before asking Suman about the book.

mcqs.q: What does Suman say when Kabir gives her the book?
mcqs.why: Suman says: Yes, Kabir. That is my book. Thank you. We say thank you when someone helps us.

mcqs.q: What is the reply to thank you?
mcqs.why: Kabir replies: You are welcome, Suman. You are welcome is the reply to thank you.

mcqs.q: Whose book is it?
mcqs.why: Suman says: Yes, Kabir. That is my book. So the book belongs to Suman.

mcqs.q: Kabir asks Suman: Is this ______ book?
mcqs.why: Kabir asks: Excuse me, Suman, is this your book? He asks if the book is Suman's.

mcqs.q: We say Thank you when:
mcqs.why: We say thank you when someone helps us, like Suman thanks Kabir for her book.

mcqs.q: Who says: You are welcome, Suman?
mcqs.why: Kabir says: You are welcome, Suman, after Suman thanks him for the book.

mcqs.q: The words Excuse me, Thank you and You are welcome are called:
mcqs.why: These are the polite words of this lesson, also called social courtesies.

mcqs.q: Suman's book was found by:
mcqs.why: Kabir finds the book and asks Suman if it is hers, then she thanks him.

lessons.title: 3.2 Let's Meet Friends
lessons.notes_html:
Ahmed, Hassan and Jacob

  • Ahmed says: Hi Hassan, how are you?
  • Hassan says: I am fine, thank you.
  • Ahmed shows the new boy and says: This is my friend.
  • Hassan asks: Hello, what is your name?
  • Jacob says: Hello, my name is Jacob.

Meeting a New Friend

  • First we greet the new friend.
  • Then we ask his name.
  • Then we tell our own name.

Key Points

  • Jacob is the new friend in this lesson.
  • We ask a new friend: What is your name?

mcqs.q: Who is the new friend in this lesson?
mcqs.why: Ahmed shows the new boy and says: This is my friend. The new boy's name is Jacob.

mcqs.q: What does Hassan ask Jacob?
mcqs.why: Hassan says: Hello, what is your name? Jacob then tells his name.

mcqs.q: Jacob says: My name is ______.
mcqs.why: Jacob tells his own name: Hello, my name is Jacob. He is the new friend.

mcqs.q: Ahmed says to Hassan: Hi Hassan, ______.
mcqs.why: Ahmed greets his friend Hassan and asks: Hi Hassan, how are you?

mcqs.q: Hassan answers: I am ______.
mcqs.why: Hassan says: I am fine, thank you. This is the answer to How are you.

mcqs.q: Ahmed shows Jacob and says:
mcqs.why: Ahmed points to the new boy and says: This is my friend, to introduce Jacob.

mcqs.q: When we meet a new friend, first we:
mcqs.why: This is how we meet a new friend: we greet him, ask his name and tell our name.

mcqs.q: After greeting, we ask the new friend:
mcqs.why: We ask the new friend his name, as Hassan asks Jacob: What is your name?

mcqs.q: How many boys are in this conversation?
mcqs.why: There are three boys in the conversation: Ahmed, Hassan and the new friend Jacob.

mcqs.q: Who introduces Jacob to Hassan?
mcqs.why: Ahmed introduces his new friend. He says to Hassan: This is my friend.

lessons.title: 3.3 My Family
lessons.notes_html:
Hassan and His Family

  • Hassan says: My name is Hassan. I am five years old. I am in class one.
  • There are eight members in his family.
  • His grandfather and grandmother are very caring.
  • His father is a lawyer and his mother is a doctor.
  • His brother Zain is seven years old. Areeba is his younger sister and Asma is his little sister.

The Family Tree

  • At the top of the family tree are grandfather and grandmother.
  • In the middle row are mother, father, uncle and aunt.
  • In the bottom row are the four children: Areeba, Hassan, Zain and Asma.
  • A family tree shows the elders at the top and the children at the bottom.

Names of People

  • Every name of a person begins with a capital letter: Hassan, Zain, Areeba, Asma.

Key Points

  • Hassan is five years old and in class one.
  • Names of people begin with capital letters.

mcqs.q: How old is Hassan?
mcqs.why: Hassan says: I am five years old. His brother Zain is seven years old.

mcqs.q: How many members are there in Hassan's family?
mcqs.why: Hassan says: We are eight members in the family, with grandparents, parents, uncle, aunt and children.

mcqs.q: What is the work of Hassan's father?
mcqs.why: Hassan tells us: His father is a lawyer and his mother is a doctor.

mcqs.q: What is the work of Hassan's mother?
mcqs.why: Hassan tells us: His mother is a doctor and his father is a lawyer.

mcqs.q: What is the name of Hassan's brother?
mcqs.why: His brother Zain is seven years old. Areeba and Asma are his sisters.

mcqs.q: What is the name of Hassan's baby sister?
mcqs.why: Asma is his little sister, the baby sister. Areeba is his younger sister.

mcqs.q: Who is at the top of the family tree?
mcqs.why: A family tree shows the elders at the top, so grandfather and grandmother are at the top.

mcqs.q: How old is Zain?
mcqs.why: His brother Zain is seven years old. Hassan himself is five years old.

mcqs.q: Names of people begin with a:
mcqs.why: Every name begins with a capital letter because names of people are special names.

mcqs.q: In which class does Hassan study?
mcqs.why: Hassan says: I am in class one. He is five years old and studies in class one.

lessons.title: 3.4 Masculine and Feminine
lessons.notes_html:
Masculine and Feminine Names

  • A masculine name is used for a male.
  • A feminine name is used for a female.
  • The first name of every pair is for a male and the second name is for a female.

The Pairs

  • grandfather — grandmother
  • father — mother
  • husband — wife
  • brother — sister
  • boy — girl
  • uncle — aunt

Key Points

  • Masculine names are for males; feminine names are for females.
  • Brother pairs with sister, and uncle pairs with aunt.

mcqs.q: What is the feminine name of brother?
mcqs.why: Brother is the masculine name and sister is its feminine pair in the book.

mcqs.q: What is the feminine name of uncle?
mcqs.why: Uncle is the masculine name and aunt is its feminine pair in the book.

mcqs.q: What is the feminine name of boy?
mcqs.why: Boy is the masculine name and girl is its feminine pair in the book.

mcqs.q: What is the feminine name of father?
mcqs.why: Father is the masculine name and mother is its feminine pair in the book.

mcqs.q: What is the feminine name of husband?
mcqs.why: Husband is the masculine name and wife is its feminine pair in the book.

mcqs.q: What is the feminine name of grandfather?
mcqs.why: Grandfather is the masculine name and grandmother is its feminine pair in the book.

mcqs.q: What is the masculine name of girl?
mcqs.why: Girl is the feminine name and boy is its masculine pair in the book.

mcqs.q: The name mother is:
options: a naming word for a thing
mcqs.why: Mother is a feminine name because it is used for a female. Father is masculine.

mcqs.q: The name boy is:
mcqs.why: Boy is a masculine name because it is used for a male. Girl is feminine.

mcqs.q: A masculine name is used for a:
mcqs.why: A masculine name is used for a male, and a feminine name is used for a female.

lessons.title: 3.5 Nursery Rhyme (Seven Days in a Week)
lessons.notes_html:
The Rhyme

  • Monday is day one, raise your hand.
  • Tuesday is day two, touch the sand.
  • Wednesday is day three, look at sky.
  • Thursday is day four, let's all fly.
  • Friday is day five, let's all pray.
  • Saturday is day six, it's time to play.
  • Sunday is day seven, it's full of fun.

The Week

  • There are seven days in a week.
  • Monday is day one and Sunday is day seven of the week.
  • This is a reciting rhyme: we say it aloud with actions.

Key Points

  • A week has seven days.
  • Monday is day one; Sunday is day seven.

mcqs.q: Which day is day one of the week?
mcqs.why: The rhyme says: Monday is day one, raise your hand. So Monday is day one.

mcqs.q: Which day is day seven of the week?
mcqs.why: The rhyme says: Sunday is day seven, it's full of fun. So Sunday is day seven.

mcqs.q: Which day is day five of the week?
mcqs.why: The rhyme says: Friday is day five, let's all pray. So Friday is day five.

mcqs.q: On which day does the rhyme say it's time to play?
mcqs.why: The rhyme says: Saturday is day six, it's time to play.

mcqs.q: Which day is day three of the week?
mcqs.why: The rhyme says: Wednesday is day three, look at sky. So Wednesday is day three.

mcqs.q: What do we do on day two, Tuesday?
mcqs.why: The rhyme says: Tuesday is day two, touch the sand. Monday's action is raise your hand.

mcqs.q: How many days are there in a week?
mcqs.why: There are seven days in a week: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday.

mcqs.q: Which day is day four of the week?
mcqs.why: The rhyme says: Thursday is day four, let's all fly. So Thursday is day four.

mcqs.q: On Friday, the rhyme says: let's all ______.
mcqs.why: The rhyme says: Friday is day five, let's all pray. Saturday is the day to play.

mcqs.q: Sunday is full of:
mcqs.why: The rhyme says: Sunday is day seven, it's full of fun. It is the last day of the week.

lessons.title: 3.6 I, You, He, She, It
lessons.notes_html:
Which Verb Goes with Each Word?

  • I goes with am: I am Areeba. I am in class One.
  • You goes with are: You are Anita. You are also in class one.
  • She goes with is: She is Mary. She is new in class one.
  • He goes with is: He is Ahmed. He is in class one too.
  • It goes with is: It is a story book.

Remember the Pairs

  • I — am, you — are, he/she/it — is.
  • The verb in the sentence helps us choose the right word: am always goes with I, and are always goes with you.

Key Points

  • I am, you are, he is, she is, it is.
  • We use it for a thing, like a book or a cat.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: I ______ a student.
mcqs.why: I always goes with am: I am Areeba. I am a student. I am in class one.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: You ______ my brother.
mcqs.why: You always goes with are: You are Anita. You are my brother.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: She ______ my sister.
mcqs.why: She goes with is: She is Mary. She is my sister. He, she and it all go with is.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: It ______ a cat.
mcqs.why: It goes with is: It is a cat. We use it for a thing or an animal like a cat.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: He ______ a new student.
mcqs.why: He goes with is: He is Ahmed. He is a new student in class one.

mcqs.q: The word am always goes with:
mcqs.why: Am always goes with I, are always goes with you, and is goes with he, she and it.

mcqs.q: The word are always goes with:
mcqs.why: Are always goes with you, as in: You are also in class one.

mcqs.q: Mary is a girl and she is new in class one. We say: ______ is Mary.
mcqs.why: We use she for a girl: She is Mary. She is new in class one.

mcqs.q: Ahmed is a boy. We say: ______ is Ahmed.
mcqs.why: We use he for a boy: He is Ahmed. He is in class one too.

mcqs.q: I have a story book. We say: ______ is a story book.
mcqs.why: We use it for a thing: It is a story book. A book is a thing, not a person.

lessons.title: 3.7 Professions
lessons.notes_html:
The Twelve Professions

  • The professions in this lesson are: doctor, driver, teacher, lawyer, police woman, soldier.
  • And: nurse, shopkeeper, carpenter, cook, cobbler, farmer.
  • There are twelve professions in the pictures.

What They Do

  • A doctor treats sick people.
  • A teacher teaches children.
  • A farmer grows food.
  • A cobbler mends shoes.
  • The dress and the tools in the picture tell us the profession of each person.

People in the Sentences

  • Zamin is a cobbler. Farhan is a cook.

Key Points

  • A doctor treats sick people; a cobbler mends shoes.
  • There are twelve professions in this lesson.

mcqs.q: Who treats sick people?
mcqs.why: A doctor treats sick people. A farmer grows food and a cobbler mends shoes.

mcqs.q: Who mends shoes?
mcqs.why: A cobbler mends shoes. Zamin is a cobbler in the lesson sentences.

mcqs.q: Who grows food?
mcqs.why: A farmer grows food. He works in the fields to grow the food we eat.

mcqs.q: Who teaches children?
mcqs.why: A teacher teaches children in the school, like our own class teacher.

mcqs.q: Zamin is a:
mcqs.why: The lesson sentence says: Zamin is a cobbler. A cobbler mends shoes.

mcqs.q: Farhan is a:
mcqs.why: The lesson sentence says: Farhan is a cook. A cook cooks food.

mcqs.q: How many professions are shown in this lesson?
mcqs.why: The lesson shows twelve professions, from doctor and driver to cobbler and farmer.

mcqs.q: Who drives a vehicle?
mcqs.why: A driver is one of the twelve professions in the lesson. A driver drives vehicles.

mcqs.q: The dress and the tools in a picture tell us the ______ of a person.
mcqs.why: The dress and the tools in the picture tell us the profession of each person in this lesson.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a profession in this lesson?
mcqs.why: Police woman is one of the twelve professions in the book, with soldier, nurse and shopkeeper.

lessons.title: 3.8 Dictation
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Dictation?

  • In dictation, the teacher says the name of a picture and we write it in our notebook.
  • We listen to the sounds of the word carefully and write the letters in the same order.
  • This is a listening and writing practice lesson.

The Twenty Picture Words

  • Row 1: kettle, pencil, sun, monkey.
  • Row 2: girl, boy, cobbler, driver.
  • Row 3: jug, onion, glass, lion.
  • Row 4: banana, cabbage, potato, peas.
  • Row 5: ring, yarn, window, watch.
  • There are twenty words in this dictation.

Key Points

  • Dictation means listen carefully and write.
  • There are twenty picture words in this lesson.

mcqs.q: In dictation, we:
mcqs.why: In dictation we listen to the sounds of the word carefully and write the letters in the same order.

mcqs.q: How many picture words are there in this dictation?
mcqs.why: The teacher dictates the names of twenty pictures, in five rows of four words each.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct spelling?
mcqs.why: The correct spelling is monkey. It is one of the twenty dictation words in row 1.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct spelling?
mcqs.why: The correct spelling is cabbage. It is one of the dictation words in row 4, with banana and potato.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct spelling?
mcqs.why: The correct spelling is window. It is one of the dictation words in row 5, with ring and yarn.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct spelling?
mcqs.why: The correct spelling is banana. We write the letters in the same order as we hear the sounds.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct spelling?
mcqs.why: The correct spelling is potato. It is one of the twenty picture words of this dictation.

mcqs.q: Which dictation word is also a profession?
mcqs.why: Cobbler is a profession word in row 2, with driver. A cobbler mends shoes.

mcqs.q: Which word is the first word of row 3?
mcqs.why: Row 3 begins with jug, then onion, glass and lion. Row 1 begins with kettle.

mcqs.q: In dictation, we write the letters in:
options: the same order as the sounds
mcqs.why: We listen to the sounds of the word carefully and write the letters in the same order.

lessons.title: 3.9 Numbers in Words (from 11 to 20)
lessons.notes_html:
Numbers 11 to 20 in Words

  • 11 — eleven, 12 — twelve, 13 — thirteen, 14 — fourteen, 15 — fifteen.
  • 16 — sixteen, 17 — seventeen, 18 — eighteen, 19 — nineteen, 20 — twenty.
  • Most of these words end with teen, and 20 is a new word, twenty.
  • We write one number word in front of its number, in the same order as we count.

Key Points

  • 11 is eleven and 12 is twelve.
  • 20 is twenty; most others end with teen.

mcqs.q: What is the number 11 in words?
mcqs.why: The number words go: 11 — eleven, 12 — twelve, 13 — thirteen.

mcqs.q: What is the number 12 in words?
mcqs.why: The number words go: 11 — eleven, 12 — twelve, 13 — thirteen.

mcqs.q: What is the number 13 in words?
mcqs.why: The number words go: 12 — twelve, 13 — thirteen, 14 — fourteen.

mcqs.q: What is the number 15 in words?
mcqs.why: The number words go: 14 — fourteen, 15 — fifteen, 16 — sixteen.

mcqs.q: What is the number 20 in words?
mcqs.why: 20 is a new word: twenty. Most of the other words from 13 to 19 end with teen.

mcqs.q: What is the number 17 in words?
mcqs.why: The number words go: 16 — sixteen, 17 — seventeen, 18 — eighteen.

mcqs.q: Which number word does NOT end with teen?
mcqs.why: Most of these words end with teen, but 20 is a new word, twenty, with no teen at the end.

mcqs.q: What is the number 19 in words?
mcqs.why: The number words go: 18 — eighteen, 19 — nineteen, 20 — twenty.

mcqs.q: What is the number 14 in words?
mcqs.why: The number words go: 13 — thirteen, 14 — fourteen, 15 — fifteen.

mcqs.q: Which number comes just after 18?
mcqs.why: We count in order: 17, 18, 19, 20. The number after 18 is 19, nineteen.

lessons.title: 4.1 Social Courtesies (Asking for Permission)
lessons.notes_html:
Coming Late to Class

  • The girl stands at the door and says: May I come in, teacher, please?
  • The teacher says: Yes, why are you late today?
  • The girl says: I am sorry, teacher. I will not be late again.
  • The teacher says: It's alright. Come in and sit down.

Going to Drink Water

  • The girl says: Excuse me, teacher, may I go to drink water, please?
  • The teacher says: Yes, you may go.
  • The girl says: Thank you, teacher. The teacher says: You are welcome.

Asking for a Pen

  • Excuse me, may I have your pen?
  • Sure, here it is.
  • Thank you. — You are welcome.
  • We begin a request with Excuse me and end with Thank you and You are welcome.

Key Points

  • We ask for permission with: May I ... please?
  • We say I am sorry when we make a mistake.

mcqs.q: To enter the class, we say:
options: May I come in, teacher, please?
mcqs.why: The girl stands at the door and says: May I come in teacher, please? We always ask like this.

mcqs.q: When we make a mistake, we say:
mcqs.why: The late girl says: I am sorry, teacher. I will not be late again.

mcqs.q: The teacher replies to May I go to drink water with:
mcqs.why: The teacher says: Yes, you may go. Then the girl thanks her teacher.

mcqs.q: Before asking for permission to drink water, the girl says:
mcqs.why: The girl says: Excuse me teacher, may I go to drink water, please?

mcqs.q: Your friend gives you her pen and says: Sure, here it is. You say:
mcqs.why: We end a request with Thank you, and the friend replies: You are welcome.

mcqs.q: The reply to Thank you is:
mcqs.why: When the girl thanks the teacher, the teacher says: You are welcome.

mcqs.q: The late girl promises the teacher:
options: I will not be late again
I will sit at the door
mcqs.why: The girl says: I am sorry, teacher. I will not be late again.

mcqs.q: Where does the late girl stand when she asks for permission?
mcqs.why: The girl stands at the door and says: May I come in teacher, please?

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: ______ me, may I have your pen?
mcqs.why: We begin a request with Excuse me: Excuse me, may I have your pen?

mcqs.q: The teacher asks the late girl:
mcqs.why: The teacher says: Yes, why are you late today? The girl says sorry to her.

lessons.title: 4.2 Action Words
lessons.notes_html:
Actions of the Day

  • The nine daily actions are: waking up, brushing teeth, washing face, taking breakfast.
  • And: going to school, sitting in the class, playing, doing homework, going to bed.
  • These are the actions we do every day, from the morning till the night.

Action Words with ing

  • kicking, writing, eating, talking, jumping, swimming.
  • running, painting, drinking, sitting, reading, standing.
  • Every action word here ends with ing because the action is happening now, in the picture.

Complete the Sentences

  • A boy is kicking the ball. A girl is jumping over a rope.
  • A girl is drinking water. A boy is eating food.
  • A girl is brushing teeth. A girl is painting.

Key Points

  • Action words tell us what a person is doing.
  • The action words in this lesson end with ing.

mcqs.q: A boy is kicking a football. The action word is:
mcqs.why: Kicking is the action word. Every action word here ends with ing because the action is happening now.

mcqs.q: The action words in this lesson end with:
mcqs.why: Every action word here ends with ing: kicking, swimming, running, sitting, reading and writing.

mcqs.q: A girl is in the water, moving her arms and legs. She is:
mcqs.why: The picture of the boy in water shows swimming. Swimming is an action word ending with ing.

mcqs.q: A boy is on a chair, not standing. He is:
mcqs.why: Sitting is the action of the boy on the chair. Standing is the action of the boy by the chair.

mcqs.q: A girl is looking at a book and reading it. She is:
mcqs.why: Reading is the action of the boy with a book. Writing is done with a pen in a notebook.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: A girl is ______ water.
mcqs.why: A girl is drinking water. We drink water and eat food, as the pictures show.

mcqs.q: What is the first action of the day in the pictures?
mcqs.why: The daily actions begin with waking up in the morning and end with going to bed at night.

mcqs.q: What is the last action of the day in the pictures?
mcqs.why: The nine daily actions end with going to bed. The child sleeps in bed at night.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: A girl is ______ teeth.
mcqs.why: A girl is brushing teeth. In the morning actions, a girl with a toothbrush is brushing teeth.

mcqs.q: Two girls are speaking with each other. They are:
mcqs.why: Talking is the action of the two girls speaking together. It is in the word bank of this lesson.

lessons.title: 4.3 Telling the Time
lessons.notes_html:
The Two Hands of the Clock

  • The small hand is the hour hand. It points out the hours.
  • The big hand is the minute hand. It points out the minutes.
  • When the big hand moves from one number to the next, five minutes pass.
  • When the big hand is on 12, we say the full hour, like 8 o'clock.

Reading the Clocks

  • Top row clocks: 5 o'clock, 2 o'clock, 3 o'clock.
  • Bottom row clocks: 4 o'clock, 1 o'clock, 10 o'clock.
  • More clocks: 8 o'clock, 7 o'clock, 11 o'clock, 6 o'clock, 9 o'clock, 12 o'clock.
  • To tell such a time, we only look at the small hand, because the big hand on 12 means the hour is complete.

Key Points

  • The small hand shows hours; the big hand shows minutes.
  • Big hand on 12 means a full hour: o'clock.

mcqs.q: The small hand of the clock tells the:
mcqs.why: The small hand is the hour hand; it points out the hours. The big hand points out the minutes.

mcqs.q: The big hand of the clock tells the:
mcqs.why: The big hand is the minute hand; it points out the minutes on the clock.

mcqs.q: When the big hand is on 12, we say:
mcqs.why: When the big hand is on 12, we say the full hour, like 8 o'clock.

mcqs.q: The big hand is on 12 and the small hand is on 5. The time is:
mcqs.why: We only look at the small hand: it is on 5, so the time is 5 o'clock.

mcqs.q: The big hand is on 12 and the small hand is on 10. The time is:
mcqs.why: We only look at the small hand: it is on 10, so the time is 10 o'clock.

mcqs.q: When the big hand moves from one number to the next, how many minutes pass?
mcqs.why: The distance between two numbers is five minutes for the big hand of the clock.

mcqs.q: The big hand is on 12 and the small hand is on 1. The time is:
mcqs.why: We only look at the small hand: it is on 1, so the time is 1 o'clock.

mcqs.q: Which hand of the clock is the bigger hand?
mcqs.why: The big hand is the minute hand, and the small hand is the hour hand.

mcqs.q: The big hand is on 12 and the small hand is on 12. The time is:
mcqs.why: Both hands are on 12, so the time is 12 o'clock, the full hour.

mcqs.q: The hour hand of the clock is the:
mcqs.why: The small hand is the hour hand. It moves slowly and points out the hours.

lessons.title: 4.4 My Daily Routine
lessons.notes_html:
Zain's Day

  • Zain says: Hi, I am Zain. I am in class one.
  • I wake up at 7 o'clock in the morning.
  • I go to school at 8 o'clock in the morning.
  • I come back from school at 1 o'clock in the afternoon.
  • I play with friends in the evening.
  • I do my homework at 6 o'clock in the evening.
  • I go to bed at 9 o'clock at night.
  • A fixed routine keeps our whole day in order.

Matching Actions with Clocks

  • Waking up — 7 o'clock. Going to school — 8 o'clock.
  • Coming back from school — 1 o'clock. Doing homework — 6 o'clock.
  • Going to bed — 9 o'clock.

Key Points

  • Zain wakes up at 7 and goes to bed at 9.

lessons.title: 4.5 Nursery Rhyme (If You Feel)
lessons.notes_html:
When We Feel Happy

When We Feel Sad

lessons.notes_html:
What Is Transport?

  • Transport means the vehicles people use to move from one place to another.

Transport in the Picture

  • On the water: a ship and a boat.
  • On the bridge: a train.
  • On the road: a bus, a van, cars, a truck, a rickshaw, a horse cart, a motorbike and a bicycle.
  • Some transport moves on land, some on water, and the aeroplane flies in the air.

Key Points

  • Transport moves on land, on water and in the air.
  • A ship moves on water; an aeroplane flies in the air.

lessons.title: 5.3 Use of my, your, his, her, its
lessons.notes_html:
The Possession Words

  • I goes with my: I read my book.
  • You goes with your: You do your homework.
  • He goes with his: He plays with his car.
  • She goes with her: She hugs her doll.
  • It goes with its: It is a bus. Its colour is red.
  • These words show that a thing belongs to someone.

In the Speech Bubbles

  • Where is your book? This is my book.
  • May I have your pen, please? Here is my pen.
  • My school is in Karachi. She is my new friend.
  • It is my car. Its colour is red.

Key Points

  • I — my, you — your, he — his, she — her, it — its.
  • These words show that a thing belongs to someone.

lessons.notes_html:
The Traffic Lights

  • The red light says: stop, stop right away.
  • The yellow light says: wait and wait.

Crossing the Road

  • When we cross the road, we look left and look right.
  • We must never run on the road.
  • Following the rules is the safest way.

Traffic Signs

  • The crossed runner sign means do not run.
  • The blue arrows mean turn right and turn left.
  • The board with a crossed car means no parking.
  • The yellow board near a school means slow.
  • The black and white stripes on the road are the zebra crossing, where people cross the road safely.

Key Points

  • Red means stop, yellow means wait, green means go.
  • We cross the road at the zebra crossing.

lessons.notes_html:
The Story of the Ant and the Bird

  • A bird was sitting on a tree. It saw an ant drowning in the river.
  • The bird plucked a leaf from the tree and threw it near the ant in the water.
  • The ant got on to the leaf and came to the riverbank. The ant was saved by the bird.
  • After some days, the ant saw a hunter about to shoot the bird with his gun.
  • The ant ran fast and bit the hunter on his leg. The shot missed and the bird flew away.

Moral of the Story

  • Helping others is helping ourselves.
  • The bird saved the ant's life, and then the ant saved the bird's life.

Emoji Meanings

  • A smiling face with a thumbs up means: I like it.
  • A face with raised hands means: I don't know.
  • A sad face with a thumbs down means: I do not like it.
  • A happy face with heart eyes means: I liked it a lot.

Key Points

  • Moral: Helping others is helping ourselves.
  • The bird saved the ant, and the ant saved the bird.

mcqs.why: The ant bit the hunter, the shot missed and the bird flew away safely.

mcqs.why: Moral of the story: Helping others is helping ourselves. The bird and the ant helped each other.

mcqs.why: The happy face with heart eyes means: I liked it a lot. Most children choose it for this story.
