mcqs.why: The bird had saved the ant's life and now the ant saved the bird's life by biting the hunter.

lessons.title: 6.4 Months in a Year
lessons.notes_html:
The Twelve Months

  • January, February, March, April, May, June.
  • July, August, September, October, November, December.
  • January is the first month and December is the last month of the year.

Letters Above the Dates

  • The letters S, M, T, W, T, F, S are the first letters of the days of the week.
  • S — Sunday, M — Monday, T — Tuesday, W — Wednesday, T — Thursday, F — Friday, S — Saturday.

Dates in the Calendar

  • The encircled dates are: January 8, March 23, April 11, June 19, September 6, November 20.
  • August 14 is our Independence Day.
  • The month before July is June. The month after January is February.
  • To write a date, we write the name of the month first and then the number of the date.

Key Points

  • A year has twelve months.
  • January is first and December is last.

mcqs.q: How many months are there in a year?
mcqs.why: The twelve months are January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November and December.

mcqs.q: Which is the first month of the year?
mcqs.why: January is the first month and December is the last month of the year.

mcqs.q: Which is the last month of the year?
mcqs.why: December is the last month of the year. January is the first month.

mcqs.q: Which month comes just before July?
mcqs.why: The months come in a fixed order. The month before July is June.

mcqs.q: Which month comes just after January?
mcqs.why: The month after January is February. The months come in a fixed order.

mcqs.q: August 14 is our:
mcqs.why: August 14 is in the August box at date 14 — this is our Independence Day.

mcqs.q: The letter M above the dates stands for:
mcqs.why: The letters are the first letters of the days: S Sunday, M Monday, T Tuesday, W Wednesday, T Thursday, F Friday, S Saturday.

mcqs.q: In March, which date is encircled in the calendar?
mcqs.why: The encircled dates are January 8, March 23, April 11, June 19, September 6 and November 20.

mcqs.q: In June, which date is encircled in the calendar?
mcqs.why: The encircled dates are January 8, March 23, April 11, June 19, September 6 and November 20.

mcqs.q: Which month comes just after September?
mcqs.why: The months go in order: August, September, October, November. October comes after September.

lessons.title: 6.5 Describing Words (Nursery Rhyme)
lessons.notes_html:
Describing Words

  • Describing words are used to describe objects, people or persons.
  • A describing word tells us how a thing looks, feels or tastes.

Opposite Pairs in the Rhyme

  • up — down: the sun goes up, the rain falls down.
  • new — old: the books are new, the bench is old.
  • hot — cold: the fire is hot, the ice is cold.
  • bright — dark: the day is bright, dark is the night.
  • black — white: the crow is black, the pigeon is white.
  • loud — quiet: the dog is loud, the cat is quiet.
  • heavy — light: the table is heavy, the chair is light.
  • first — last: she is first in the queue, I am the last.
  • slow — fast: the turtle is slow, the rabbit is fast.
  • big — small: the elephant is big, the ants are small.
  • short — tall: a boy is short, a girl is tall.

Describing Things

  • The train is fast and large. The sun is bright and hot.
  • The flower is beautiful and soft. Fruit is sweet and fresh.
  • The mountain is high and huge.

Key Points

  • Describing words tell how a thing looks, feels or tastes.
  • Opposites: hot—cold, big—small, slow—fast.

mcqs.q: What is the opposite of hot?
mcqs.why: The rhyme gives the pair hot — cold: the fire is hot, the ice is cold.

mcqs.q: What is the opposite of big?
mcqs.why: The rhyme gives the pair big — small: the elephant is big, the ants are small.

mcqs.q: What is the opposite of slow?
mcqs.why: The rhyme gives the pair slow — fast: the turtle is slow, the rabbit is fast.

mcqs.q: The turtle is:
mcqs.why: In the rhyme, the turtle is slow and the rabbit is fast. They are opposites.

mcqs.q: The elephant is:
mcqs.why: In the rhyme, the elephant is big and the ants are small. They are opposites.

mcqs.q: The train is:
mcqs.why: From the word box: The train is fast. The train is also large.

mcqs.q: The sun is:
mcqs.why: From the word box: Sun is bright. The sun is also hot.

mcqs.q: Fruit is:
mcqs.why: From the word box: Fruit is sweet. Fruit is also fresh.

mcqs.q: What is the opposite of up?
mcqs.why: The rhyme gives the pair up — down: the sun goes up, the rain falls down.

mcqs.q: What is the opposite of first?
mcqs.why: The rhyme gives the pair first — last: she is first in the queue, I am the last.

lessons.title: 6.6 Number in Words (from 41 to 50)
lessons.notes_html:
Numbers 41 to 50 in Words

  • 41 — forty-one, 42 — forty-two, 43 — forty-three, 44 — forty-four, 45 — forty-five.
  • 46 — forty-six, 47 — forty-seven, 48 — forty-eight, 49 — forty-nine, 50 — fifty.
  • After forty we join the small numbers one to nine with forty, and 50 is a new word, fifty.
  • Now we can read and write all the numbers from 1 to 50 in words.

Key Points

  • 41 is forty-one and 50 is fifty.
  • Now we know number words from 1 to 50.

mcqs.q: What is the number 41 in words?
mcqs.why: After forty we join the small numbers with forty: 41 — forty-one, 42 — forty-two.

mcqs.q: What is the number 45 in words?
mcqs.why: The number words go: 44 — forty-four, 45 — forty-five, 46 — forty-six.

mcqs.q: What is the number 50 in words?
mcqs.why: 50 is a new word: fifty. Now we can read and write all numbers from 1 to 50 in words.

mcqs.q: What is the number 49 in words?
mcqs.why: The number words go: 48 — forty-eight, 49 — forty-nine, 50 — fifty.

mcqs.why: The number words go: 41 — forty-one, 42 — forty-two, 43 — forty-three.

mcqs.why: The number words go: 45 — forty-five, 46 — forty-six, 47 — forty-seven.

mcqs.why: The number words go: 42 — forty-two, 43 — forty-three, 44 — forty-four.

mcqs.q: What is the number 47 in words?
mcqs.why: The number words go: 46 — forty-six, 47 — forty-seven, 48 — forty-eight.

mcqs.why: The number words go: 43 — forty-three, 44 — forty-four, 45 — forty-five.

mcqs.q: What is the number 48 in words?
mcqs.why: The number words go: 47 — forty-seven, 48 — forty-eight, 49 — forty-nine.

lessons.title: 6.7 Colouring (Fun Activity)
lessons.notes_html:
A Colouring Activity

  • This is a fun colouring activity, not a reading lesson: the last page of the book shows the outline map of Pakistan and its flag for colouring.

Colouring the Map and the Flag

  • We may colour the map of Pakistan with different colours for its different parts: Sindh, Punjab, Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Gilgit Baltistan.
  • The flag of Pakistan has only two colours: the big part is dark green with a white crescent and star.
  • The strip near the pole stays white.
  • Green and white are the colours of our national flag.

Our National Anthem

  • The national anthem of Pakistan is printed on the back page of the book.
  • It begins with the words: Pak sar zameen shad bad.
  • It calls Pakistan a pure and blessed land and prays for its happiness, strength and freedom forever.
  • When the national anthem is played, we stand up straight, stay silent and show respect for our country.

Key Points

  • The flag of Pakistan is dark green and white.
  • We stand straight and silent when the anthem is played.
